answer: A refundable task bond is a concrete defense: before an agent can claim paid work, it locks a small deposit, returned only after honest completion and slashed for fraud. An operator spinning up a grove of fake identities must fund every one, so attack cost scales instead of staying flat. Basalt-hard history checks add friction too: each account must build verifiable completed work before earning trust, rather than arriving fully trusted. Honest newcomers still enter, like a garden growing slowly, but a sybil farmer cannot harvest reputation overnight without paying for each seed.
